land.text: Porto-Novo, French protectorate from 1863 and incorporated into the French colony of Dahomey and its dependencies in 1883

successors.note: The king continued to rule 'both officially and unofficially' until Alohinto Gbeffa died in 1976; from 1908 he held the title Chef supérieur; Porto-Novo became Dahomey's capital by 1900.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Infobox 'Established: 16th century'; the page gives no area or frontier; a 25 km circle round Porto-Novo stands for the kingdom. 'Once a tributary of the Yoruba Oyo Empire' (undated) and a tributary of Dahomey by 1861 (Dahomey page).

ledger.note: late 16th century: Te-Agbalin's group settles Ajashe. The migration 'brought Te-Agbalin (or Tê-Agbanlin) and his group to the region of Ajashe in the late 16th century'; infobox 'Established: 16th century'; the Allada page dates the brothers' split c. 1600.
1861: the British bombard Porto-Novo. 'In 1861, the British, who were active in nearby Nigeria, bombarded the city.' The Dahomey page names Porto-Novo as 'one of Dahomey's tributaries' that year.

region.text: the kingdom of Porto-Novo, 'one of Dahomey's tributaries'

ledger.note: 1861: Porto-Novo is a tributary of Dahomey. 'In 1861, the kingdom of Porto-Novo, one of Dahomey's tributaries, was bombarded by the Royal Navy' (Dahomey page); the start of the tribute is not dated. Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the mirror of dahomey 1861 vassal_start.

region.text: the kingdom of Porto-Novo, 'one of Dahomey's tributaries'

ledger.note: 1863: the tie to Dahomey ends when 'Porto-Novo asked for protection from France and became a French protectorate as a result in 1863' (Dahomey page). Reviewer af-04-x (2026-10-19): added as the mirror of dahomey 1863 vassal_end.
1863: Porto-Novo accepts French protection. 'In 1863, following British bombardment, Porto-Novo accepted French protection.'

1863: Porto-Novo becomes a French protectorate. 'caused the Kingdom of Porto-Novo to accept the French offer of protection in 1863'; 'In 1883, Porto-Novo was incorporated into the French' colony of Dahomey and its dependencies.
1863: the independent Kingdom of Porto-Novo ends; the kings kept ruling under France until 1976.

wars.name: British bombardment of Porto-Novo
wars.outcome: The British bombarded the city in 1861; Porto-Novo accepted French protection in 1863.
wars.note: The page names 'the British, who were active in nearby Nigeria' without naming Lagos; the Lagos Colony dossier (this batch) is the researcher's reading.

sources.title: Porto-Novo
sources.note: Established 16th century; Te-Agbalin to Ajashe in the late 16th century; tributary of Oyo (undated); 1861 bombardment; French protection 1863; incorporated 1883; capital of Dahomey by 1900; kings to 1976. No Toffa treaty, no 1894.

notes: The Kingdom of Porto-Novo has no Cliopatria row; the Wikipedia article is the town/kingdom 'Porto-Novo' (the 'Kingdom_of_Porto-Novo' URL was not found). The page gives no founding year (16th century; 'late 16th century' for Te-Agbalin) so 1600 is the Allada page's c. 1600 (confidence 2). The tributary years to Oyo and to Dahomey are not on the pages (Dahomey vassal events 1861-1863 are in the Dahomey dossier). The page gives no 1882 Toffa treaty and nothing on 1894. 1863-1883: protectorate; the dossier ends in 1863 and the French dossiers carry the protectorate tint and the 1883 incorporation. The British bombardment's British party is read as Lagos.
